On ending Ukraine war Norway, Finland leaders hold 'frank and substantive' talk with Putin
AFP
Published: 27.10.26 12:01 , Update: 27.10.26 12:55
The Finnish, Norwegian and Ukrainian leaders in Oslo last week
© NTB/AFP
Finland's president and Norway's prime minister held a "frank and substantive" discussion with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Tuesday about efforts to end the war in Ukraine, the Nordic leaders said.
"The outcome of this war will have a direct impact on our and the broader European security. Ending the war requires direct discussions", President Alexander Stubb said in a joint statement with Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store.
The statement noted that the call had been "held in consultation with Ukraine" and followed a meeting in Oslo on October 20 between Store, Stubb and Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky as well as US envoy Steve Witkoff.
US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner also took part in the meeting remotely.
After the Oslo talks, Witkoff travelled to Saint Petersburg to meet Putin.

Bombe in Müssen gefunden? Bahnstrecke Hamburg-Berlin gesperrt
Stand: 27.10.2026 • 11:01 Uhr
In Müssen ist möglicherweise eine Bombe gefunden worden. Anwohner sollen unverzüglich ihre Wohnungen zu verlassen. Die Bahnstrecke wurde gesperrt: Der Bahnverkehr zwischen Hamburg und Berlin sowie Hamburg und Schwerin ist unterbrochen.
Aufgrund eines möglichen Bombenfunds müssen Anwohnerinnen und Anwohner der Bergstraße und Bahnhofstraße in Müssen ( Kreis Herzogtum Lauenburg ) spontan ihre Haushalte verlassen. Das teilte die örtliche Gefahrenabwehrbehörde der Gemeinde Müssen heute Vormittag mit. Auch einige Gebäude im näheren Umfeld wurden evakuiert.
Kampfmittelräumdienst kommt aus Kiel
Entdeckt wurde der verdächtige Gegenstand gegen 8.40 Uhr im Bereich einer Baustelle am Bahnhof Müssen, so die Polizei. Bisher handelt es sich bei der Bombe nur um einen Verdacht, es könnte sich demnach um einen Sprengkopf handeln. Ob es sich tatsächlich um einen Munitionsfund handelt, muss laut Polizei der Kampfmittelräumdienst klären, der alarmiert wurde. Er sei bereits auf dem Weg…

titulek: Leaders of Finland and Norway talk to Putin
titulekPuvodni: Leaders of Finland and Norway talk to Putin
shrnuti: Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian PM Jonas Gahr Støre initiated the call to discuss efforts to end the Ukraine war.

vyrez.text:
Leaders of Finland and Norway talk to Putin – POLITICO
Skip to main content
Advertisement
Finland’s President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre held a joint call with Russian leader Vladimir Putin on Tuesday as part of international efforts to secure an end to the war in Ukraine.
“The discussion was frank and substantive,” said Stubb said in a statement after the call. “We are neighboring countries to Russia. The outcome of this war will have a direct impact on our and the broader European security. Ending the war requires direct discussions.”
The two leaders — who are firm allies of Ukraine — were not speaking as official representatives of Europe as a whole. The call was held in consultation with Ukraine.
Støre said the European leaders stressed the importance of de-escalation in the call with Putin. “The war comes with enormous human and material costs. The suffering and destruction will impact generations,” he added.
Their conversation comes at a highly sensitive moment as U.S. President Donald Trump pushes for a peace deal. Talks between the U.S., Russia and Ukraine are planned to take place in Abu Dhabi next month.

A truce has begun in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky, a week after it was announced by US First Lady Melania Trump.
Ukrainian officials and Russia's defence ministry both say the limited ceasefire is being respected. The ceasefire is meant to allow aid deliveries and the evacuation of civilians, which has been planned for Friday.
Oleshky is trapped between the Dnipro River, which forms the front line in the Kherson region and separates it from Ukrainian positions, and Russian forces.

Italian army removes and defuses 250 explosives encased in ice for more than 100 years after hikers’ sightings
A significant cache of unexploded bombs from the first world war emerged this summer from rapidly retreating glaciers in the Dolomites, the Italian army has said.
The devices, which included Italian artillery shells and French mortar bombs, were removed and defused by the army’s Julia Alpine brigade, according to a statement.
The weapons originated from the white war, a battle between the Austro-Hungarian army and Italian troops across treacherous and bitterly cold terrain between 1915 and 1918.

Alexander Kondratov, the production designer for the Russian TV series Likvidatsiya (Liquidation”), has died at Botkin Hospital in Moscow after being arrested on treason charges, the Russian human rights group Department One said.

Kondratov was born and raised in Moscow but had lived in Kyiv since 2012. He had traveled to Russia to renew his foreign passport and was detained at Vnukovo Airport. Moscow mother of eight charged with financing terrorism over payment to ISIS
October 26, 2026, 8:33 am
Source: Meduza
Maria Davydova, a 31-year-old Moscow mother of eight, has been arrested on charges of financing terrorism.
The case was opened in July under Russia’s criminal statute against financing terrorism, and a court authorized her arrest. Davydova was added to Russia’s list of terrorists and extremists.
Citing a source in law enforcement, the Russian state news agency RIA Novosti reported in July that investigators believe Davydova transferred about 15,000 rubles to the Islamic State.
Case materials cited by the Russian state news agency TASS on October 26 state that Davydova “is self-employed, has eight dependent children, including young children and minors, is not married, and has a specialized secondary education.”
Russia’s criminal statute under which Davydova is charged allows for a sentence of up to life in prison.
A military court will hear Davydova’s case. The trial’s start date has not been announced.

Čas 4.36 v sobotu ráno rozhodně není momentem, kdy by poslanci řešili zákony. Vládní koalice si pro svůj výpad proti veřejnoprávním médiím ale vybrala právě tento okamžik.
Změnu financování ČT a rozhlasu začaly špičky Babišovy koalice řešit silově a také překvapivě – a to až tak, že o tom předem neřekly ani vlastním poslancům.
Noční jednání tak provázely hádky, porušování zvyklostí i ohýbání jednacího řádu. A také protesty veřejnosti. Během celého jednání probíhala demonstrace v okolí Sněmovny, protesty pokračují také během víkendu.
V nové epizodě podcastu Vrtěti psem situaci probíráme s reportérkami Zdislavou Pokornou a Karolínou Blažkovou, které sledovaly jednání přímo na místě – v budově Sněmovny i v místě protestů.
Rozebíráme také, proč Babiš vůbec celou akci spustil.

LÆS OP
ORDBOG TEKST
Af
Jonas Foldager
Aleksander Boelt Bruun
I dag kl. 07:00
Over 40.000 mennesker søgte ned i Kyivs metro under Ruslands massive angreb i sommer. 
For over et år siden begyndte Metroselskabet at undersøge, om Københavns metro også kunne bruges som beskyttelsesrum, sådan som det sker i Kyiv.
Dengang lød det, at undersøgelsen ville være færdig inden for få måneder, men resultaterne fra arbejdet har endnu ikke set dagens lys.
Nu afslører hidtil fortrolige mails mellem Københavns Kommune og Metroselskabet, som DR har fået aktindsigt i, at metroen i dag ikke kan bruges som beskyttelsesrum.
I hvert fald ikke uden omfattende ændringer.
Det bekræfter Lene Sandberg, lektor ved Københavns Professionshøjskole. Hun forsker i samfundssikkerhed,…

Kyiv's power ring under attack: why the capital faces a winter of blackouts | Ukrainska Pravda
Hopes for a mild winter or inaccuracies in Russian strikes will not help Kyiv get through this winter without problems with its electricity supply. The only question is how long the power cuts will last and whether air defence forces and power engineers will manage to prevent the worst-case scenario.
The Russians are continuing their systematic attacks on Kyiv and Kyiv Oblast, seeking to completely destroy the city's combined heat and power plants and break the so-called power ring in order to plunge the capital entirely into darkness and cold.
The city has already lost a significant proportion of its own power generation capacity, while strikes are destroying substations through which electricity is supplied from other regions. In the event of severe frosts and further hits, a scenario involving 20 hours without electricity no longer seems far-fetched.

Despite downgrade consensus, the agency kept France's sovereign rating unchanged, a short-lived relief, say economists, warning of a debt time bomb and worsening political and social tensions.
An unexpected piece of good news: Moody's has left France's sovereign debt rating untouched. Although markets had widely expected a downgrade, the New York-based agency on Friday evening maintained its assessment at Aa3 with a negative outlook.
ADVERTISEMENT
ADVERTISEMENT
France's ten-year borrowing rate (OAT) has soared this week, while the country is under strain after the riots of 17 October, which have added to investor unease. Moody's nevertheless justified its stance in a statement, explaining that "the Aa3 rating is based on the assumption that a 2027 budget reducing the deficit will be adopted, while funding costs and social tensions will moderate somewhat over the coming months".

The US has declared helium a critical material as war in the Middle East and export curbs by Russia and China squeeze global supplies of a gas vital to chipmaking, leaving Europe scrambling to secure its share.
The United States designated helium as a critical material on Friday, citing its essential role in semiconductor manufacturing and energy production, as well as growing concerns over disruptions to global supplies.
ADVERTISEMENT

The move by the US Department of Energy will make additional federal funding available to helium producers and bring the material under closer government monitoring.
Helium is mainly extracted as a byproduct of natural gas processing. The US is the world's largest producer of both natural gas and helium, with Qatar and Russia also among the leading helium producers.

Ukrainian forces launched a missile attack on Russia’s Oryol region. Preliminary reports from Ukrainian monitoring channels suggest the target was the Proton factory, which produces optoelectronic equipment and components for military use.
A missile alert was issued across the Oryol region at about 5 p.m. local time. Local Telegram channels reported at least four explosions in the city of Oryol. Afterward, residents reported seeing thick smoke and hearing emergency vehicles.
Storm Shadow cruise missiles were used in the attack on Oryol, according to preliminary reports from Ukrainian monitoring channels.
The Telegram channel Exile+ reported that the factory’s products are used to manufacture S-71 “Kover” air-launched cruise missiles, 9M723 Iskander-M ballistic missiles, and Pantsir-S1 air defense missile and gun systems.

Russia and the U.S. have both denied that Russia had released American national Stephen Hubbard from prison in exchange for the recent release of a Russian war blogger detained in Montenegro whom the U.S. has accused of election interference.
Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Wednesday that Hubbard, a 74-year-old U.S. citizen held in Russian custody since 2022, had been freed in what the Kremlin called a humanitarian goodwill gesture.
U.S. President Donald Trump said he had asked Putin to free Hubbard and that Russia had not asked for anything or anyone in return for letting the retired U.S. schoolteacher return home.

Romania said Friday that one sailor had died and three were missing after a drone struck and sank a ship in the Black Sea, with the country's president blaming Russia for the attack.
The cargo ship Khoryv, flying the Comoros flag, was "struck by a drone and sank near Romanian territorial waters," President Nicușor Dan wrote in a Facebook post.
Speaking to reporters, Dan said the attack was "clearly part of the escalation that Russia is carrying out in the context of the war in Ukraine."
Romania launched a rescue operation after the Khoryv sent a distress signal around 10:00 am local time, 13 nautical miles from the Romanian port of Constanta.
Romanian authorities said 10 Ukrainian and three Azerbaijani crewmembers were on board.

Mit dem anhaltenden Angriffskrieg Russlands auf die Ukraine häufen sich auch die Vorfälle hybrider Kriegsführung in Europa. Immer wieder melden nicht nur Russlands Nachbarstaaten etwa Sabotageakte, Drohnenangriffe und GPS-Störungen. Ein Recherchenetzwerk der European Broadcasting Union (EBU), dem auch der ORF angehört, hat nun die Vorfälle gesammelt. Fachleute sehen die Grenze zwischen Krieg und Frieden zunehmend verschwimmen.

Die Ukraine nutzt das Satellitennetzwerk für ihre Abwehr Russlands. Source: RMF24
Officers from Poland’s Internal Security Agency have detained a 22-year-old Georgian citizen in connection with the murder of Russian performance artist Semyon Skrepetsky, said Tomasz Siemoniak, the coordinator of Poland’s intelligence services.
RMF24 identified the man as Makhmud A. The outlet reported that he helped the suspected killer, who had been detained earlier, by keeping Skrepetsky’s home under surveillance and gathering information about his habits.
Makhmud A. arrived in Poland the day before he was detained and was traveling with two other Georgian citizens. The other two were expelled from the country, RMF24 reported.
Makhmud A. was charged with aiding and abetting murder and illegally possessing weapons and ammunition. He denied the charges.
Russian performance artist Semyon Skrepetsky was killed on June 15 in the Polish city of Biała Podlaska. The first suspect in his murder was detained near Warsaw on June 18.…

Germany detains Ukrainian national suspected of spying for Russia
October 22, 2026, 3:24 pm
Source: Reuters
A Ukrainian citizen, Vadym Y., was detained in the German state of Brandenburg on suspicion of spying for Russia, Germany’s federal prosecutor’s office said.
According to investigators, the suspect had been in contact with Russian intelligence services through an intermediary since no later than July 2025. Prosecutors believe he collected military intelligence, including information on the production of armored vehicles, ammunition, and explosives, as well as on personnel and military facilities in areas intended to ensure the security of NATO’s eastern flank.
Some of this information was publicly available, while other information was obtained from representatives of the European defense industry.
The court is expected to consider a motion to place the suspect in pretrial detention on October 23.

A retired US teacher freed by President Vladimir Putin after four years' detention in Russia for allegedly fighting on behalf of Ukraine has returned to the United States, his lawyer said Thursday.
"Yes he has landed back," Stephen Hubbard's lawyer Martin De Luca told AFP, without providing details.
US President Donald Trump posted photos early Thursday showing Hubbard smiling as he posed with US special envoy Steve Witkoff.
Another photo showed the former English teacher, who is in his 70s, posing with unidentified people on a small plane, holding up an American flag with two members of the group.

Russian law enforcement authorities have arrested former State Duma lawmaker from the Communist Party Oleg Mikhailov on charges of publicly justifying terrorism, his regional party team said Wednesday.
Mikhailov has headed the Communist Party branch in the northern republic of Komi since 2014 and served as a State Duma member between 2021 and September 2026. In last month’s parliamentary elections, he lost his seat to a rival from the ruling United Russia party.
Komi’s Communist Party branch said in a social media post that Mikhailov was arrested at a Moscow airport after returning from a vacation.
The charge against Mikhailov of publicly justifying terrorism stems from old social media posts in which he allegedly supported jailed sociologist Boris Kagarlitsky and leftist activist Sergei Udaltsov .

Starosta Moskvy Sergej Sobjanin na síti Telegram později uvedl, že na Moskvu v noci mířilo zhruba 630 dronů. Informoval o dvou zraněných.

Článek
V Kyjevě zasáhly ve čtvrtek v časných ranních hodinách rakety, uvedl svědek agentury Reuters . Jedná se o další útok na ukrajinské hlavní město, který následoval po večerním ruském leteckém úderu, při kterém bylo zraněno šest lidí.
Při předchozím útoku byla v Dniprovském obvodu poškozena autoservisní stanice a soukromý obytný dům, informoval starosta Vitalij Kličko. Dodal, že pod sutinami mohou být uvězněni lidé.

Japan sent a senior diplomat to Moscow this week to discuss the release of a journalist arrested in Russia on spying accusations, Tokyo said Wednesday.

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has denied that Japan conducts spying activities in Russia, while the Hokkaido Shimbun has stressed its independence from the government.

Russian scientist convicted of treason refuses food and water over alleged abuse in detention
October 21, 2026, 4:57 pm
Source: Department One
Valery Kachin, a geodesist from Birobidzhan who was sentenced in January 2025 to 14 years in a penal colony for treason, has begun a dry hunger strike at Pretrial Detention Center No. 1 in Izhevsk, the human rights group Department One (Pervy Otdel) reported.
In a letter from the detention center, Kachin, 39, said he had stopped eating and drinking after staff tormented and physically assaulted him. He said he has been held continuously in a punishment cell: After an initial seven days, he was given another 10 days, followed by two consecutive 15-day terms. He said staff force him to raise and lower a heavy bed by himself, even though he is not required to do so. He said staff also conduct nighttime inspections and confiscate personal belongings from his cell.
